stories.title: Tyson Fury to be assessed by boxing chiefs
stories.summary: The British Boxing Board of Control is evaluating Tyson Fury ahead of his 11 December fight against Anthony Joshua. The assessment follows revelations in a Netflix documentary regarding the boxer's past mental health struggles. His wife, Paris, has clarified that he has never received a diagnosis of schizophrenia.

stories.title: Paris Fury clarifies boxer's mental health diagnosis
stories.summary: Paris Fury says her husband, Tyson Fury, has never received a medical diagnosis of schizophrenia. The clarification follows promotional clips for a forthcoming Netflix documentary in which she referred to the boxer having mild schizophrenia. Netflix has edited the film ahead of its 27 November release.

The clarification follows promotional clips for a forthcoming Netflix documentary in which she referred to the boxer having mild schizophrenia. stories.title: Tyson Fury Reveals He Heard ‘Demonic’ Voices and Thought His Own Family Was Plotting Against Him During Mental Health Cr
Canadian TV host shares update on depression
stories.summary: Ainsley McPhail, a television presenter in Winnipeg, has announced she is likely experiencing depression following a doctor's assessment. The update comes after the reporter previously shared her bipolar disorder diagnosis. She is now offering tips for others navigating similar mental health challenges.

stories.title: Long waits for neurodevelopmental assessments in Scotland
stories.summary: More than 38,000 adults in Scotland are waiting for ADHD and autism assessments, with at least 14,000 waiting longer than two years. Dr. Marianne McCallum described the backlog as a tragedy, noting that demand now far exceeds the capacity of the current mental health system.

stories.title: NHS faces challenges with ADHD and autism assessments
stories.summary: The NHS is experiencing significant difficulties in providing timely ADHD and autism assessments. Experts suggest that rising demand has outpaced the capacity of the mental health system, leading to long waiting lists for patients seeking a diagnosis.

stories.title: Parents' mental health linked to child wellbeing
stories.summary: A 2024 U.S. Surgeon General's advisory found that 48 percent of parents report feeling stressed on most days. Researchers suggest that efforts to improve children's wellbeing have historically focused on the children themselves, potentially overlooking the impact of parental mental health on the family unit.

stories.title: Vidya Balan calls for action on child sexual abuse
stories.summary: Actor Vidya Balan has urged the public to stop treating child sexual abuse as a peripheral issue. She advocates for a proactive approach that prioritizes listening to and believing survivors, rather than looking away from the reality of the problem.

stories.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media habits
stories.summary: A University College London review of 43 studies involving 28,000 participants suggests that higher levels of mindfulness are associated with healthier social media use. The findings, published in PLOS One, indicate that mindful individuals report lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness, and fear of missing out.

stories.title: How Gratitude Meditation Can Support Mental Health and Help You Feel Happier - Verywell Mind
Managing expectations during social gatherings
stories.summary: Hosting social events often involves significant time and financial investment, which can lead to unexpected stress. Experts suggest that ignoring difficult feelings during these moments can exacerbate frustration, particularly when faced with last-minute guest requirements or hurtful comments from family members.

stories.title: Researchers propose framework for art therapy
stories.summary: Authors Juliet L. King, Johanna Czamanski-Cohen, and Matthew Pelowski have published a framework in Nature Mental Health to clarify the clinical scope of art therapy. The authors aim to resolve current ambiguity and improve evidence synthesis for the regulated mental health profession.

stories.title: Mindfulness may mitigate social media impacts
stories.summary: A University College London review of 43 studies involving 28,000 participants suggests that mindfulness may help users manage the negative effects of social media. The research, published in PLOS One, links higher mindfulness levels to lower reports of anxiety, depression, stress, and fear of missing out.

stories.title: Mindfulness associated with better mental health outcomes
stories.summary: A systematic review of 43 quantitative studies published in PLOS One found that higher mindfulness is linked to healthier social media engagement. Researchers from University College London noted that participants reported less social comparison and reduced compulsive platform use when practicing non-judgmental awareness.

stories.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use
stories.summary: A University College London-led review published in PLOS One found that higher levels of mindfulness are associated with healthier social media habits. The study, which assessed 28,000 participants, suggests mindfulness may help buffer the mental health effects of digital platforms, including stress and loneliness.

stories.title: Review links mindfulness to social media experience
stories.summary: Researchers at University College London analyzed 43 studies involving 28,000 people and found that higher mindfulness is associated with better mental health indicators. The review, published in PLOS One, covered participants aged 10 to 92 and suggests mindfulness can lead to healthier social media use.

stories.title: Mindfulness may protect mental health from social media
stories.summary: A University College London-led review published in PLOS One suggests that higher levels of mindfulness are associated with healthier social media use. The study of 28,000 participants found that mindful individuals report lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, and the fear of missing out.

stories.title: Can You "Overdo" Healthy Sleep? Trackers, Melatonin, and the Trap of Perfect Rest - LIGA.net
Vitamin D levels linked to better sleep in adults over 40
stories.summary: A Johns Hopkins study found higher vitamin D levels associated with longer, less interrupted sleep in adults aged 40 and older. The findings add to existing research on the relationship between vitamin D and sleep quality, though they do not establish that the vitamin directly improves sleep.

stories.title: Aging may disrupt brain fluid circulation during sleep
stories.summary: A study published in Nature Aging reports that as individuals grow older, the movement of cerebrospinal fluid surrounding the brain weakens during sleep. This fluid cushions the brain and transports substances, and researchers suggest this decline may interfere with processes essential for maintaining long-term brain health.

stories.title: Stable sleep patterns show non-significant link to liver disease
stories.summary: A longitudinal study published in BMC Gastroenterology found that stable, long-term sleep disturbances do not show a significant trend toward increasing the risk of developing metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. The research evaluated sleep duration and latency over a five-year period in a population-based cohort.

stories.title: Pilot study tests contactless vital sign monitoring in children
stories.summary: Researchers in Germany have introduced a protocol to integrate contactless sensing systems into routine paediatric sleep studies. The team aims to address the high technical requirements and limited scalability of traditional polysomnography, which remains the gold standard for evaluating sleep health in children despite its obtrusive setup.

stories.title: Post-concussion insomnia triples recovery time for youth
stories.summary: A study from an Australian pediatric hospital found that children with persistent post-concussion symptoms and clinical insomnia require a median recovery time of 150 days. This is three times longer than the recovery period for patients who do not experience sleep disturbances following a concussion.

stories.title: Winter insomnia may mask underlying sleep apnea
stories.summary: Hana ENT Hospital suggests that persistent difficulty falling asleep during winter months should be evaluated for sleep apnea rather than dismissed as simple seasonal insomnia. The hospital notes that treating only one condition can be ineffective, as the two often create a cycle that worsens overall health.

stories.title: Higher vitamin D levels associated with longer sleep
stories.summary: A study of 460 adults found those with the highest vitamin D levels slept an average of 20 minutes longer per night than those with the lowest. The association, based on blood tests and actigraphy data, appeared strongest among Black participants in the study group.

stories.title: Very low-dose antidepressant shows potential for chronic insomnia
stories.summary: A retrospective case series suggests that doses of mirtazapine far below those used for depression may help patients with chronic insomnia. Researchers reported that more than 75 percent of patients in the study were able to discontinue conventional sleeping medications while using the very low-dose treatment.

stories.title: Manual farm work as a substitute for gym training
stories.summary: Amanda Owen, who manages a 2,000-acre farm, describes her daily manual labour as a substitute for a structured gym programme. The work involves rebuilding walls and managing livestock, which Owen notes is physically strenuous and serves as a functional, if back-breaking, fitness regime.

stories.title: No-equipment workout targets strength for runners
stories.summary: A 30-minute bodyweight routine has been developed to target major muscle groups without the need for gym equipment. The workout is intended for runners and those with busy schedules, providing a series of exercises that can be performed in any location to improve strength.

stories.title: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental health
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 104 studies found emotional abuse in childhood more strongly associated with adult depression and anxiety than physical or sexual abuse. The researchers noted that these findings are based on adult memories and do not establish cause or rank the severity of different abuse types.

stories.title: Tai Chi may reduce insomnia in older adults
stories.summary: A systematic review published in Aging Clinical and Experimental Research indicates that Tai Chi can reduce insomnia severity and daytime sleepiness in middle-aged and older adults. The practice is being evaluated as a non-pharmacological intervention for sleep disturbances that often accompany the aging process.

stories.title: Foam roller exercises suggested for core strength
stories.summary: Malaika Arora suggests that five foam roller moves can be used to build core strength. The routine is presented as an alternative to performing a large number of different exercises, focusing on simple movements to target the abdominal muscles.

stories.title: Strength training linked to longevity and functional independence
stories.summary: Research indicates that lower-body strength training is associated with a reduction in all-cause mortality. A 2026 study further suggests that women benefit from increased resilience and functional independence through regular strength training, highlighting the role of muscle health in both the quantity and quality of life.

stories.title: Exercise during hemodialysis may improve physical strength
stories.summary: A meta-analysis in the American Journal of Nephrology found that combining aerobic and resistance exercise during hemodialysis sessions can improve physical activity levels and oxygen consumption. The study suggests that the intensity and duration of the exercise program are key factors in achieving these specific outcomes.

stories.title: Awareness of Home Exercises and Shoulder Stiffness in Community-Dwelling Adults Aged 60 Years and Older: A Cross-Section
Fitness tech gifts for recovery and performance
stories.summary: A range of wellness gadgets, including red light therapy and muscle stimulation tools, are marketed to athletes for recovery and performance tracking. These devices are designed to provide data on metrics such as heart rate, blood oxygen, and sleep quality to assist with personalized training insights.

stories.title: Two-thirds of Indian adolescents are vitamin B12 deficient
stories.summary: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, according to an ICMR survey. The study found deficiency in 66.1 percent of boys and 65.4 percent of girls. The nutrient is described as essential for brain development, nerve function, and red blood cell formation.

stories.title: Does Pea Protein Raise Blood Sugar? What the Evidence Shows for Everyday Wellness - Comité Asesor de Vacunas de la AEP
Turmeric shot study tracks gut bacteria in footballers
stories.summary: Researchers from UK institutions followed 11 professional footballers for six months to test the effects of turmeric shots. Findings published in Performance Nutrition indicated an increase in Blautia bacteria, which the study links to anti-inflammatory effects. Eight players took the supplement while three served as a control.

stories.title: Low Zinc May Let Gut Bacteria Eat Away at Your Gut Lining - Dr. Axe
Delhi study finds low dietary diversity in pregnant women
stories.summary: A clinical assessment at Delhi's Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital found that only 35.7 percent of pregnant participants met thresholds for adequate dietary diversity. The study evaluated women in their first half of pregnancy to determine if maternal body mass index correlated with the variety of foods consumed.

stories.title: Study finds gap in urban protein awareness
stories.summary: A YouGov study of eight Indian cities found that only 59 percent of urban consumers recognise milk as a complete protein. While 60 percent consume milk daily via tea or coffee, 40 percent drink it plain. Most respondents consider milk an affordable protein source.

stories.title: Exercise linked to longevity more than diet
stories.summary: A review in Mayo Clinic Proceedings suggests physical activity has a stronger association with lower mortality than dietary quality. Researchers at Arizona State University and Kaiser Permanente concluded that daily movement may carry more weight than eating patterns. Movement is now the primary metric for longevity.

stories.title: Want to Live Longer? One Thing Is More Important Than a Healthy Diet - Inc.com
Psychiatrists suggest gratitude for mental health
stories.summary: Psychiatrist Dr. Gail Saltz suggests that practicing gratitude year-round can help mental health, strengthen relationships, and increase longevity. The comments follow a discussion on the potential benefits of maintaining a grateful outlook, which experts suggest may support health as individuals age.

stories.title: Harvard study links gratitude to longevity in women
stories.summary: A 2024 Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health study of 49,275 women found that those with higher scores on a gratitude questionnaire had lower mortality rates. The research followed participants with an average age of 79 to observe how the habit supports healthy aging.

stories.title: Harvard study identifies strength training range for longevity
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing data from 147,000 adults found a specific weekly range of resistance training linked to the largest drops in mortality risk. The study spans 30 years of data, aiming to clarify how much lifting is required to see longevity benefits. The target is described as doable.

stories.title: The Longevity Nutrient in Fatty15 Gains Three Big Wins Across Heart, Metabolic, and Cognitive Health - Lelezard
Zulal Wellness Resort launches longevity retreat
stories.summary: The Zulal Wellness Resort has introduced a Golden Longevity Retreat, a personalised journey for adults to invest in long-term health. The resort claims the program supports needs ranging from building resilience in midlife to maintaining mobility in later years. The focus is on healthspan rather than just lifespan.

stories.title: Dolphin social predictability increases with age
stories.summary: A study published in PLOS Biology suggests that social predictability in dolphins increases as they age. The author, Erin R. Siracusa, proposes this behavioral shift as a potential marker of longevity. The research was funded by a Royal Society University Research Fellowship.

stories.title: Exercise outweighs diet in longevity review
stories.summary: A review by Arizona State University and Kaiser Permanente researchers published in Mayo Clinic Proceedings indicates that physical activity is more closely linked to reduced all-cause mortality than dietary quality. The findings suggest that cardiorespiratory fitness may be a more significant factor in living longer.

stories.title: Psyched Wellness provides strategic review update
stories.summary: Psyched Wellness continues to evaluate strategic alternatives, including debt or equity financing, strategic partnerships, or the sale of company assets. The life sciences firm focuses on products derived from the Amanita Muscaria mushroom. The company is currently reviewing its ongoing financing requirements.

stories.title: Acupuncture and the search for calm
stories.summary: The Bradden Method combines facial acupuncture with reiki, reflexology, and LED therapy to reset the nervous system. While the treatment is marketed for its facelift effect and radiant glow, one user reported a deep sense of calm and a natural high after the session.

stories.title: Defining art therapy as a clinical profession
stories.summary: A new perspective in Nature Mental Health aims to clarify art therapy as a regulated profession. The authors argue that the current use of art therapy as an umbrella term obscures clinical scope and complicates evidence synthesis for researchers and practitioners in the field.

stories.title: AIIA Treats Over 37.74 Lakh Patients in a Decade, Expands Ayurveda Healthcare Reach - DD News
Acupuncture study targets cancer-related fatigue
stories.summary: A randomized clinical trial of 221 breast cancer survivors found that a structured course of acupuncture significantly reduced persistent fatigue compared to usual care. The study, published in Integrative Medicine Research, focused on patients suffering from symptoms for at least six months after completing cancer treatment.

stories.title: Trial protocol investigates massage for cancer fatigue
stories.summary: Researchers at Yueyang Hospital have launched a clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of one-finger meditation massage for cancer-related fatigue. The study aims to measure physical, emotional, and cognitive exhaustion in breast cancer patients, noting that the condition often fails to resolve with standard rest.

stories.title: Aromatherapy studied for procedural anxiety
stories.summary: A study published in Pain Management Nursing suggests that aromatherapy, particularly lavender, may reduce procedural anxiety. The authors describe the practice as a safe, nonpharmacologic adjunct to support patient well-being, provided that nursing staff implement the treatment according to established safety guidelines.

stories.title: Mirasa Ayurveda targets national wellness expansion
stories.summary: Co-founder Jasmine Kaur Basu is expanding Mirasa Ayurveda beyond Delhi, aiming to build a national wellness brand. The company intends to combine traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with personalized care and sustainable growth strategies to make the healthcare system more accessible to a wider market.

stories.title: Trial protocol tests electroacupuncture for stroke recovery
stories.summary: A multicenter trial in Hangzhou is evaluating whether electrical stimulation added to acupuncture improves cognitive recovery in stroke survivors. The study involves 340 participants across five medical centers and aims to address cognitive impairment that frequently emerges following acute cerebrovascular events.

research.title: Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging
research.summary: Researchers have uncovered a kidney protein that may hold an important key to vascular aging and longevity. The protein helps prevent excess phosphate from accumulating in the blood and gradually turning flexible blood vessels rigid. In animal models, a deficiency accelerated blood vessel aging and significantly shortened lifespan.
